name: Ford 289 small-block V8, GT40 Mk I race specification with 180-degree 'bundle of snakes' headers
summary: Cross-plane pushrod V8 whose crossover headers take two pipes from each bank into each collector, so every collector sees evenly spaced 180-degree pulses; that turns the usual V8 burble into a smooth, high flat-plane-like howl.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found on an opened page.

compression_ratio.note: GT40 Mk I competition engine. Road K-code 289 HiPo: 10.5:1 (enginefacts.com, fordmuscle.com); road-going GT40: 9.0:1 (same supercarnostalgia page).

firing_order.note: Wikipedia calls this the 'usual' small-block order (351W and 5.0 HO differ); enginefacts.com lists 15426378 for every 289. Ford numbers each bank sequentially (Wikipedia, Firing order); the same article says Ford puts cylinder 1 on the right bank, flagged citation-needed. So: 1-2-3-4 right bank front to rear, 5-6-7-8 left bank.

crank.value: cross-plane: four throws at 90 degrees, each pin shared by one cylinder from each bank
crank.note: General cross-plane description from Wikipedia; Burns Stainless describes the GT40's engine as a 90-degree-crank V8.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Even 90 degrees engine-wide. Per bank it is uneven (my calculation from the firing order and Ford numbering): right bank fires 1, 4 after 180, 2 after 90, 3 after 180, 1 after 270; left bank fires 5, 6 after 270, 7 after 180, 8 after 90, 5 after 180.

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 1.780 in. CarTech: all production 289 heads, including High Performance, share these valve sizes. Race GT40 heads may have been modified; no race-engine valve size was found.

intake_lift_mm.note: K-code 289 HiPo solid-lifter cam, NOT confirmed as the GT40 race cam: 0.460 in total valve lift with 1.6:1 rockers.

intake_duration_deg.note: K-code HiPo cam, ADVERTISED duration (lift basis not stated, seat-to-seat style figure). Not confirmed for the GT40 race engine.

le_mans_cam_lobe_lift_mm.note: Ford 'Le Mans' cam C7FE-6250-A sold through the Muscle Parts catalogue: manufacturer spec 0.330 in LOBE lift intake and exhaust; the article also quotes '216 degrees duration at .100-inch lift' from the original specs. Whether the Le Mans-winning GT40s ran exactly this grind is not established by the source.

peak_power_kw.note: 380 bhp at 6500 rpm for the FAV competition Mk I with four Weber 48 IDA. Converted by me. Revs Institute lists its GT40 Mk I at 390 hp at 7000 rpm; K-code road engine 271 hp at 6000.

peak_torque_nm.note: 330 lb-ft at 5500 rpm; converted by me. K-code road engine: 312 lb-ft at 3400.

redline_rpm.note: Not found. Power peaks quoted at 6500-7000 rpm.

intake_type.value: individual throttles: four twin-choke Weber 48 IDA downdraught carburettors, one barrel per cylinder

throttle_dia_mm.note: Carburettor is the Weber 48 IDA; barrel and choke (venturi) dimensions were not read on an opened page.

header_type.value: 180-degree crossover '4-1 x 2' (bundle of snakes): two pipes from each bank cross over the engine into each of two 4-into-1 collectors
header_type.note: Burns Stainless: 'two tubes from each bank of the V-8 are crossed over the engine to collect in 4-1 collectors', 'resulting in four evenly spaced exhaust pulses as in the flat-crank header design'.

header_collector_grouping.note: DERIVED BY ME, not read off a drawing: with firing order 1-5-4-2-6-3-7-8 at 90 degrees, every second cylinder (1,4,6,7) is 180 degrees apart, as is the other set (5,2,3,8). With Ford numbering that is cylinders 1 and 4 (right bank, end cylinders) plus 6 and 7 (left bank, middle cylinders) into one collector, and 5 and 8 (left bank ends) plus 2 and 3 (right bank middle) into the other; so the middle two cylinders of each bank are the ones that cross over. This satisfies Burns Stainless's and Wikipedia's description (two tubes from each bank per collector, 180-degree intervals). A search-result summary of gt40s.com forum posts gave the same (1467)/(5238) grouping and said the centre-pair tubes cross over, but the forum blocked fetching, so that corroboration is unverified. One poster there reportedly noted at least one original car whose headers do not cross over.

primary_length_mm.note: No published length for original GT40 headers found. A gt40s.com thread (archived copy) says most existing GT40 headers have unequal-length primaries and a builder asks hypothetically about 32 in versus 28 in; that is a forum question, not a measurement.

primary_dia_mm.note: 1 5/8 in primaries on Schoenfeld REPLICA 180-degree headers, from a gt40s.com forum post (archived copy). Forum source, replica part; original GT40 primary diameter not found.

missing: race-engine cam specification as actually run in GT40s (only K-code and catalogue Le Mans cam data found)
Weber choke size and intake stack length
original header primary length and diameter
a drawing or factory statement of which cylinder goes to which collector (grouping here is derived)

sources.what: Supercar Nostalgia guide to the GT40 Mk I (1965). Bore, stroke, displacement, 10.0:1, 380 bhp at 6500, 330 lb-ft at 5500, Webers.
Revs Institute museum page for its GT40 Mk I. 90-degree pushrod V8, four Webers, 390 hp at 7000 rpm.
Wikipedia, Ford small block engine. 289 bore and stroke, firing order, HiPo section.
CarTech Books excerpt, 'Ford Small-Block General Data and Specifications'. Valve sizes for all 289 heads, HiPo details.
FordMuscle K-code rebuild article, part I. HiPo cam lift and advertised duration, 271 hp at 6000, 312 lb-ft at 3400, valve sizes.
FordMuscle K-code article, part II. Le Mans cam part number and lobe lift.
enginefacts.com 289 table. Firing order and ratings per variant.
Burns Stainless (race exhaust fabricator) article on bundle-of-snakes 180-degree headers. How the crossover works and why.
Wikipedia, Crossplane. Per-bank intervals; GT40 bundle of snakes collecting 180-degree intervals in each branch.
Wikipedia, Firing order. Ford's per-bank sequential numbering.
Archived gt40s.com forum thread 'Header Primary Lengths'. Forum posts: unequal-length primaries on most GT40 headers; 1 5/8 in replica primaries.

name.note: Motor Sport, September 1965, on the production GT 40 with the 289 race engine. This vehicle block serves both defs ford_289_gt40 and ford_289_gt40_180 (same engine and car; only the headers differ).

curb_kg.note: Quote: "The total weight of the car is 2,000 lb. (17.85 cwt.)". Basis not stated. Others: supercarnostalgia (https://supercarnostalgia.com/blog/ford-gt40-mk1-65) "typically weighed in at 910kg"; gt40.org.uk (https://www.gt40.org.uk/GT40/GT40_Versions.htm) "Weight at scrutineering: 2440 lbs"; Revs Institute chassis 1049 "1835 lbs".

gear_count.note: Quote: "five-speed DS25 all-synchromesh unit from ZF in Germany". Motor Sport Sep 1965: "5-speed Z.F. gearbox built in Germany".

gears.note: Quote: "With gearbox ratios of 2.42, 1.47, 1.09, 0.96 and 0.85". Car tested: road-equipped GT40P/1013, which the article calls "identical to the Group 4 racing versions". Inference (ours): supercarnostalgia's in-gear maxima, "71mph (first), 117mph (second), 159mph (third), 181mph (fourth) and 204mph (fifth)", are in the proportions of this set.

final_drive.note: Quote: "Final drive 4.22:1 or 3.33:1." Choice ours: with 0.85 x 3.33 on the estimated tyre radius, supercarnostalgia's 204 mph in 5th comes at about 7,350 rpm; with 4.22 it would need about 9,300 rpm.

tyre.note: Rear. Quote: "Borrani wire spoke, alloy rim with 5.50 x 15 in. front and 7.00 x 15 in. rear, Goodyear." Motor Sport Dec 1966 agrees: "shod with 7.00 x 15in. Goodyear tyres".

wheel_radius_m.note: ESTIMATED (ours): 7.5 in rim radius plus a section height assumed at 85% of the 7.00 in width, times 0.98. The real tyre's height ratio was not found.

top_speed_kmh.note: Period estimate, not a timed figure. Quote: "were capable of 190m.p.h. down the Mulsanne straight at Le Mans". gt40.org.uk: "Top speed: 200 mph".

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Ford GT40' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: MR layout (mid-engine, rear-wheel drive).
